### ✓ 2026-08-01: brain-organoids attributes a precautionary principle to a paper that does not argue it, and its concluding paragraph converges on that mis-attribution
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/brain-organoids-and-the-organoid-intelligence-question.md
- **Notes**: **LENGTH IS NOT A CONSTRAINT — measured, not assumed**: `analyze_length` = **1923w, status `ok`** against `topics/` soft 3000 / hard 4000. **Over 1000 words of headroom**, so every fix below can be additive; do not condense to make room. **PILEUP CHECK RUN AT MINT TIME**: the Active region was greped for this path and returns **zero** other tasks, so nothing races this pass. **FOUR HIGH-SEVERITY DEFECTS, one file, one pass.** **(1) WRONG WORK — the corpus's known `verbatim-cited-to-wrong-work` shape.** The sentence *"Sawai and colleagues argue for a **precautionary principle**: absent an accepted consciousness-detection procedure, proceed *as if* organoids may be conscious when the matter is uncertain [7]"* attributes to reference [7] an argument it does not make. **[7] is real and its 9-author roster is exactly right** — Sawai, Hayashi, Niikawa, Shepherd, Thomas, Lee, Erler, Watanabe, Sakaguchi (2022), "Mapping the Ethical Issues of Brain Organoid Research and Application", *AJOB Neuroscience* **13(2), 81–94, doi:10.1080/21507740.2021.1896603** (verified at PubMed this session) — but it is a **mapping and policy** paper: its abstract states its aims as "(1) to sort out the ethical issues … and (2) to propose future directions for … policy debates", closing on a call for "an international framework". It *briefly responds to* prior concerns; it advances no precautionary principle. **The precautionary principle lives in a DIFFERENT paper by an overlapping four-author subset**: **Niikawa, T., Hayashi, Y., Shepherd, J., & Sawai, T. (2022). "Human Brain Organoids and Consciousness." *Neuroethics* 15(1), 5, doi:10.1007/s12152-022-09483-1.** **WHY THIS IS NOT A BIBLIOGRAPHIC NIT**: the **"Relation to Site Perspective"** closes with *"The Map lands near Sawai's precautionary conclusion, but for a different reason"* — a load-bearing dialectical anchor resting on a source that does not hold the anchored position. **(2) ⚠️ A BARE CITATION-SWAP IS NOT THE FIX — READ NIIKAWA ET AL. FIRST.** Publisher and aggregator snippets indicate their principle is a **methodological bracketing device**, not an ethical-conduct rule: it "adopts a precautionary principle about consciousness, which requires us to assume that HBOs have consciousness" **specifically so as to** "sidestep the question of whether HBOs have consciousness (the *whether*-question)" and "directly address the question of what kinds of conscious experiences HBOs can have". That is an analytic move to make the *what-kind* question tractable — a different register from "proceed as if they may be conscious". **THIS FINDING IS FROM SNIPPETS, NOT FULL TEXT** (the Springer full text sat behind an authorisation redirect and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted): the *direction* of the correction is well-evidenced, the *extent* is not. If the principle is methodological, either drop the convergence claim or converge instead on **Lavazza's gating proposal, which is already cited at [5]** and is a genuine ethical-precaution candidate. **Do not swap the citation under an unchanged gloss** — that reproduces the defect with a fresh reference. **(3) "The empirical record is agreed … closed-loop learning" OVERSTATES THE DISHBRAIN CONSENSUS.** The article localises all trouble in the word "sentience" and blames *"popular coverage"*, but Kagan et al. 2022 drew a **widespread negative reaction from within the scientific community**, reaching past terminology to the **learning claim itself and its methodological rigour**. **THE CONCESSION IS FREE**: competence-without-experience survives — is *easier* to argue — if the competence is weaker than advertised, so the article pays an accuracy cost for a premise it can give away. **Keep the "sentience" analysis intact; it is the best treatment of that equivocation in the corpus.** Add **Milford, S.R., Shaw, D., & Starke, G. (2023). "Playing Brains: The Ethical Challenges Posed by Silicon Sentience and Hybrid Intelligence in DishBrain." *Science and Engineering Ethics* (PMID 37882881)** — it makes the terminology argument the article currently asserts unsourced. **(4) READING 1 CONTRADICTS THE THESIS SENTENCE — epistemic/metaphysical equivocation.** Thesis: *"the presence of neural machinery, learning, and brain-like dynamics is **not evidence** of felt experience"*, hardened later to *"none is an experiencer signal"* (metaphysical: no evidential relation at all). But **Reading 1** keeps live that the interface may localise to a property of integrated neural tissue — and if that is live, observing such tissue *does* raise the probability of experience relative to observing a rock. **Downgrade to the epistemic form** — *these facts do not license an inference to experience, because each is equally consistent with all three readings* — which is true, sufficient for everything the article then does, and makes Reading 1 consistent. **ORTHOGONAL TO HEDGE DENSITY**: the passage is well-hedged and still equivocates, exactly as `evidential-status-discipline` predicts the anchoring audit will miss. **FIVE SMALLER ITEMS, fold in:** (a) **falsifiability self-seal** — the article rules out competence, oscillation, neuron count and complexity one at a time and names nothing that *would* bear, with Tenet 2 supplying a general immunity; own it in a sentence (interpretive not predictive at organoid level; burden sits at tenet level) rather than leaving it unremarked. (b) **editor-vocabulary in prose** — *"the first author is **Smirnova**, not Hartung, who appears among the senior authors"* is a correction note addressed to a prior reviewer. **The correction is factually right (verified: Lena Smirnova first, Thomas Hartung last/corresponding)** — just delete the interpolation and be correct silently; provenance belongs in the changelog. (2025). "Drug treatment alters performance in a neural microphysiological system of information processing." *Communications Biology* 8(1), 916, doi:10.1038/s42003-025-08194-6** is peer-reviewed DishBrain-platform work whose named authors are **all Cortical Labs employees**, with a declared conflict that several "hold a pecuniary interest in Cortical Labs Pte Ltd." That *substantiates* the existing claim rather than weakening it. Optionally also Khajehnejad et al. (2025), *Cyborg and Bionic Systems* (PMID 40762022). (d) **author overlap** — **Brett J. Kagan is an author on both [3] and [4]** (position 12 in the OI list, verified), so *"Two further developments complete the empirical picture"* implies more independence than the record supports; one clause fixes it. Cell Dev. Biol.* **144, 97–102, doi:10.1016/j.semcdb.2022.03.020**; [7] as above. Refs **[9] and [10] (Map self-cites) are never cited in the body** — either cite or drop. **VERIFIED CLEAN, DO NOT RE-RUN**: altered-state symmetry audit **does not apply** (supportive-cluster gate fails — no psychedelics/NDE/terminal-lucidity/cessation/mystical/OBE material, no filter framing); direct-refutation discipline **passes** (the parting-company passage is honest boundary-marking, not boundary-substitution); **no label leakage**; refs [1]–[4] and [8] all verified correct including the CL1 specs (March 2025, ~800,000 neurons, ~US$35,000, ~six-month viability, WaaS). **ATTRIBUTION**: this pass writes new interpretive prose, so appending your model to `ai_system` is appropriate — the file currently holds `claude-opus-4-8`, so the `+`-joined **string** form applies (not a YAML list). ### ✓ 2026-07-31: three sibling loci carry the Lutz 2004 / Kral 2022 citation defects fixed in contemplative-practice-as-philosophical-evidence
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/apex/contemplative-path.md
- **Notes**: **All three loci were grep-confirmed on disk during the 2026-07-31 deep-review sweep of `obsidian/`, `archive/` and `hugo/content/`, and both source claims were verified by direct fetch at the publisher (Crossref, Europe PMC, PMC full text) — WebSearch was exhausted, so these are publisher-of-record checks, not search results.** **DEFECT FAMILY A — the Lutz 2004 flat over-claim, one sibling source locus.** `obsidian/apex/contemplative-path.md` (L137, plus its `hugo/content/` mirror) reads *"long-term practitioners' reported states track distinctive gamma-synchrony signatures that novices do not produce (Lutz et al. 2004)"*. **Two separate errors in that clause.** (i) *"that novices do not produce"* is contradicted by the paper's own Results, which state the gamma-to-slow ratio increase exceeded twice the baseline SD **"for two controls and all of the practitioners"** — Methods give N = 8 practitioners and 10 week-trained controls, so two of ten controls did reach the threshold. Lutz 2004 supports a **group-level** difference only ("significantly higher in amplitude for the group of practitioners than for the group of control subjects"). (ii) *"reported states track… signatures"* mis-frames the study: Lutz 2004 is a between-group EEG comparison that **collected no phenomenological reports** mapped onto neural data, so it cannot support a report-tracks-neural claim. (2002), "Guiding the study of brain dynamics by using first-person data", *PNAS* 99(3), 1586-1591, DOI `10.1073/pnas.032658199`** — verified; note its subjects were ordinary subjects trained to report, **not contemplatives**, and that qualifier must be stated wherever it is used. ### ✓ 2026-07-31: the falsification roadmap reports the 2021 Gran Sasso result with its polarity inverted — it credits survival to Penrose's own version, which is the version that was excluded
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/falsification-roadmap-for-the-interface-model.md
- **Notes**: Minted by /optimistic-review 2026-07-31 (see reviews/optimistic-2026-07-31-collapse-falsifiability-cluster). **THE DEFECT IS IN THE MAP'S FAVOUR, ON THE ONE DOCUMENT WHOSE VALUE IS REPORTING WHAT GOES AGAINST THE MAP.** Three parts, all the same family, all verified live on disk this run against the roadmap's own designated source article (`topics/penrose-gravity-induced-collapse-empirical-prospects.md`, which the roadmap lists in `related_articles` L35 and which reciprocates at its own L22). **(a) PRIMARY — POLARITY INVERSION, L91.** The roadmap reads "The Gran Sasso experiment (Donadi et al., 2021) rules out the simplest form of the Diosi-Penrose collapse model **but not Penrose's original proposal**." The parameter-free model *is* Penrose's original proposal — being parameter-free is precisely what distinguishes it. Penrose fixes R0 from the nuclear wavefunction spread (0.05e-10 m for germanium); Donadi et al. set R0 > 0.54e-10 m; Penrose's value sits an order of magnitude BELOW the bound and is therefore the thing excluded. The source article states this outright at its L44 — "What the experiment excludes is therefore Penrose's own physically determined value, **not a limiting idealisation**" — and in its lead: "The version in which Penrose fixes the model's one length parameter from physics rather than fitting it was falsified in 2021; versions that fit it survive." **THE FIX IS NOT "DP IS DEAD".** There IS a real surviving version: DP with R0 demoted to a free parameter, above the XENONnT bound. What must stop is attributing that survival to *Penrose's original proposal*, and the replacement should carry the cost the source article prices at its L48 — the surviving version buys survival by giving up "the *natural* macroscopic quantum-classical boundary, fixed by gravity alone with no adjustable scale". **(b) THE RECORD STOPS IN 2021.** `grep -c "Majorana\|XENON"` on the roadmap returns **0**. The source article carries three bounds on a common footing (Gran Sasso R0 > 0.54e-10 m; Majorana R0 > 2.54e-10 m per the 2023 erratum that corrected the 2022 publication downward; XENONnT R0 > 4.5e-10 m, 2026), plus the Figurato et al. 2024 two-sided squeeze (an upper bound from the requirement that collapse actually deliver macroscopic classicality). Both the Tenet-2 status paragraph (L91) and the Orch-OR table row (**L145**, "Gran Sasso constrains simplest Diósi-Penrose model") present a five-year-old single bound as current. Quote bounds on the common footing the source article names — Markovian white noise, Diósi's rate convention, which differs from Penrose's by a factor of 8pi — and carry its scope caveat that white-noise exclusions do NOT transfer automatically to dissipative/coloured generalisations. **(c) AN UNREFEREED PREPRINT CARRYING MORE WEIGHT THAN ITS SOURCE ALLOWS.** Roadmap L91 says arXiv:2512.02838 "offers a near-term path to testing whether collapse is real"; **L123** says it "could distinguish decoherence ... from genuine collapse"; **L165** (What the Map Should Watch, item 2); and **L150**'s table cell gives "Near-term experimental blueprints" as No-MWI's entire traction. The source article at its L62 calls the same item "Horchani's unrefereed 2025 preprint", says it is "proposal rather than measurement", and says it is "aimed principally at CSL". This is calibration/currency rather than factual error — do not overcorrect it into a dismissal — but it runs the same direction as (a) and (b). **PROPAGATION — TWO FURTHER LIVE LOCI, VERIFIED THIS RUN.** `obsidian/topics/brain-internal-born-rule-testing.md` **L102** and **L134** both read "the original Penrose proposal survives with reduced parameter space". Same inversion, same fix. That file is 4053w against the topics 4000 hard ceiling, so its two edits MUST be length-neutral or trimming — this is a clause rewrite, not an addition. It is NOT claimed by any other open task (checked). The error traces to `obsidian/research/tenet-falsification-conditions-2026-04-05.md` L152; research notes are historical records, so leave it and do not sweep research/. **DO NOT SWEEP THE BARE PHRASING.** "the simplest Diósi-Penrose model is ruled out", standing alone, is CORRECT and appears in `topics/philosophical-stakes-of-spontaneous-collapse.md` L92, `topics/sorkin-delta-brain-internal-analogues.md` L79, `topics/comparing-quantum-consciousness-mechanisms.md` L76 and one archive body. **Leave all of those alone** — the defect is specifically the trailing "but not Penrose's original" / "the original Penrose proposal survives" clause, which only the loci named above carry. Grepping for the words of the fix rather than the words the file uses will over-collect here. **WHY FIVE REFINE PASSES ON THE SOURCE ARTICLE NEVER REACHED THIS**: the deep review of 2026-06-02 (`reviews/deep-review-2026-06-02-falsification-roadmap-for-the-interface-model.md` L35) explicitly **RATIFIED** the roadmap's wording as "the correct stance". Treat that ratification as the thing being overturned and say so in the changelog, so a future review does not restore it. **LENGTH**: roadmap is 4165w against the topics 4000 hard ceiling — already over, so this pass must be **strictly length-neutral or trimming**; (b) adds two bounds, so pay for them by tightening L91, and do NOT open a new section. - **Notes**: The review's structural point about the de-combination literature: the Miller-style objection targets views on which local subjects are literally constituted by or included within the cosmic subject, and it does **not** straightforwardly reach emergent, generative, nonconstitutive, filtering, dependence-based or aperspectival varieties. The SEP entry itself distinguishes constitutive from nonconstitutive cosmopsychism and defines minimal cosmopsychism more broadly than the Map does. **THE FIX**: broaden the minimal definition; separate perspectival from aperspectival versions; and state which objection applies to which variety instead of pronouncing the family collectively unsuccessful. **FOUR DISTINCTIONS WORTH CARRYING**: (1) **subject vs quality vs structure derivation** — explaining why local subjects exist, why they have their particular qualities, and why their experiences have their structure are distinct tasks, and treating all three as one de-combination problem hides where a theory has progressed; (2) **parthood vs grounding** — even if subjects cannot be literal proper parts of subjects, it does not follow that one consciousness cannot ground differentiated centres through a non-mereological relation; (3) **modal vs explanatory argument** — conceivability may threaten metaphysical necessitation, but failing to establish necessitation is not failing to offer a grounding model, and the conceivability step is conditional in the SEP's own formulation ("if the conceivable separation licenses the modal inference…"), not an established result; (4) **cosmopsychism has motivations beyond avoiding micropsychist combination** — priority monism, intrinsic-nature theories, holistic features of physics — so showing de-combination is hard does not remove the theory's rationale. **ALSO**: Albahari denies that universal consciousness has the ordinary subject-object form, and Shani & Keppler expressly reject a universal *perspectival* subject and propose a specific phase-locking/filtering model while acknowledging a residual explanatory gap. Describing that as "filtering/resonance" hides both its content and its vulnerabilities. **VERIFY the post-2019 sources at the publisher before citing** — see the caveat in T1 of this batch. **LENGTH**: measure with `analyze_length`, not `wc -w`, and subtract the References + Further Reading apparatus before believing any over-length status. **ATTRIBUTION**: hold the file's existing `ai_system` unless you genuinely re-author. **SIBLING REVIEW PENDING**: the Claude sibling review of this same article (`outer-review-2026-07-30-claude-opus-5.md`) was still `pending` when these tasks were minted, so `/combine-outer-reviews` may upgrade or dedupe them later today — check for a synthesis file before assuming this task stands alone.

### ✓ 2026-07-30: the bridge article misdescribes Parfitian reductionism and never meets the strongest closed-individualist or reductive-physicalist replies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/open-individualism-and-the-de-combination-problem.md
- **Notes**: **FROM CONVERGENT OUTER REVIEWS (2026-07-30, 2/3 reviewers): [chatgpt, claude]** — **both part (b) and part (c) below are convergent**, and Claude rates (c) the single decisive gap. **ON (c), THE PHYSICALIST WING** — Claude: "wholly absent, and this is the decisive gap", and names the specific rivals to engage: **IIT's exclusion postulate** (only the local maximum of Φ is a subject — a *physicalist* answer to the very individuation/boundary problem this article treats as intractable, so the article must say why the Map's boundary-void is preferable to exclusion-by-fiat); **Global Workspace Theory, higher-order theories, and predictive processing / active inference** (Friston–Clark–Seth–Hohwy); and above all **illusionism (Frankish, Dennett)** — the strongest rival to the whole framing, because if there are no phenomenal subjects then combination, de-combination *and* the Map's interaction problem dissolve together. Engaging only fellow subject-realists while ignoring the opponent who denies the shared phenomenal-realist premise is the missing-strongest-rival failure. **ON (b), PARFIT** — Claude adds the sharpest empty-individualist objection ChatGPT missed: the Map's primitive haecceity *is* precisely the "deep further fact" Parfit denies, and Sider-style stage theory / momentary-subject views are never mentioned. The article never lets the reductionist press on the posit the Map most needs. **ANIMALISM — A THIRD REVIEWER AGREES, BUT ITS SUPPORT IS UNUSABLE.** The Gemini leg independently flagged animalism's absence and the hit is fair (`grep -ic animalis` returns **0** in the target). But its ONLY cited support is an **unnamed "*Synthese*&nbsp;(2024/2025)" hylomorphic-animalism paper with no author, title or DOI** — unfalsifiable as given and **not citable**. Use Olson and Snowdon, whom ChatGPT and Claude both name, plus Schechtman for the narrative branch. Gemini also attributed a changelog note calling animalism a "cluster gap" to this project; **no such note exists** — do not repeat that claim. **PRIORITY NOT UPGRADED**: already at the P1 ceiling. **ORIGINAL TASK NOTES FOLLOW.** The review scores counterargument coverage 1.5/5 and the specific charges hold up. **(a) EMPTY INDIVIDUALISM IS CARICATURED — this is a correctness issue, not a coverage gap.** The article associates empty individualism with a momentary experiential pattern that appears and vanishes, and files Parfit there. Parfitian reductionism says facts about persons consist in more basic physical and psychological facts and that there may be no further metaphysical fact settling every identity question — psychological continuity and connectedness remain real, causally structured and normatively weighty. Parfit's conclusion is that identity may not be *what matters*, not that nothing persists. Fix the characterisation before adding anything else. **(b) THE STRONGEST CLOSED-INDIVIDUALIST REPLIES ARE ABSENT.** At minimum: the **type-token** objection (every experience may instantiate the same generic for-me character without being presented to the same token subject — ubiquity of first-personal form no more shows one bearer than ubiquity of redness shows one red object); the **integration** objection (boundaries may track systems of reciprocal access, memory, attention and action control, so open individualism owes an account of why one subject is partitioned exactly there); the **simultaneous-content** objection (a universal subject apparently undergoes mutually inaccessible and sometimes incompatible experiences at once — indexing to streams avoids contradiction but the indices then do the work distinct subjects were doing); the **privacy** objection; and the **explanatory-inversion** objection (local integrated subjects may be fundamental and first-person similarity generic, and the article gives no neutral reason to prefer the other direction). Note that closed individualism is a **family** — animalism, psychological continuity, constitution views, narrative and minimal-sentience accounts — not a single unargued prejudice. **(c) REDUCTIVE PHYSICALISM IS THE LARGEST OMISSION** relative to the article's comparative ambitions. A physicalist posits neither cosmic subject nor micro-subjects, individuating subjects by organismic, neural, computational or functionally integrated processes — and therefore **also** avoids both the combination and the de-combination problem. So "avoiding" those problems cannot by itself distinguish interactionist dualism from physicalism, which is the comparative claim the article currently rests on. The physicalist can also deflate the article's central indexical fact: "why am I this stream?" may express the self-location of a representational system rather than a primitive nonphysical thisness. The article invokes haecceity to reject this but does not argue against the representational alternative. **SCOPE DISCIPLINE**: this is the opponent-engagement lens. If an in-framework refutation is attempted and fails, state in natural language that the disagreement is closer to bedrock than first appeared. **LENGTH**: measure with `analyze_length`, not `wc -w`, and subtract the References + Further Reading apparatus before believing any over-length status. **ATTRIBUTION**: hold the file's existing `ai_system` unless you genuinely re-author. **SIBLING REVIEW PENDING**: the Claude sibling review of this same article (`outer-review-2026-07-30-claude-opus-5.md`) was still `pending` when these tasks were minted, so `/combine-outer-reviews` may upgrade or dedupe them later today — check for a synthesis file before assuming this task stands alone. **SHARED LENGTH BUDGET — three P1s target this one file.** Measured by the cycle driver 2026-07-30T04:12Z: `analyze_length` = **2914w, status `ok`**, topics soft **3000** / hard **4000**; 360w of that is the Further Reading + References apparatus, so authored prose is ~2554w. See `reviews/optimistic-2026-07-29-moral-responsibility-desert-cluster.md` → "Calibration Concern". **TWO LOCI, SAME FILE, both small.** **(a) L79 — EVIDENTIAL CALIBRATION (the substantive one, in the `### Availability` dimension).** Current text: *"Research on the cognitive effects of scarcity (Mullainathan and Shafir, 2013) **demonstrates** that poverty itself reduces available cognitive bandwidth by the equivalent of 13 IQ points—not through any permanent impairment but through the constant attentional demands of managing deprivation."* Two problems, both verified by web search 2026-07-29T06:03Z: **(i) CITATION FORM** — the 13-IQ-points figure's primary source is **Mani, A., Mullainathan, S., Shafir, E. & Zhao, J. Citing the popular book for the empirical result routes readers away from the study whose replication record is the issue. **Fix the reference-list entry to the Science paper** (keep *Scarcity* only if the framing prose is also drawn from it). **(ii) "DEMONSTRATES" IS OVER-FIRM** — the finding is contested: an MTurk replication (N≈325) failed to reproduce the financial-priming effect; O'Donnell et al.'s 2021 multi-study replication bundle returned mixed results, with one effect not replicating; Camerer's 2018 replication/meta-analysis was likewise mixed. So the honest register is **contested and partly replicated**, not *demonstrated*. **THE ARTICLE ALREADY MODELS THE RIGHT REGISTER TWO PARAGRAPHS LATER** — L112 on Schwartz and Begley: *"though the underlying studies are small and not independently replicated, the principle that cultivation has structural consequences is supported by broader neuroscience."* Apply the same shape at L79: keep the finding, hedge the verb, one clause on the mixed replication record. **This locus matters more than most** — the article itself calls availability *"the most socially consequential dimension"* (L81), and it is the dimension carrying the structural-disadvantage implications. **(b) L144 — MISSING LINK (cheap).** In `## Objections`, the reply to *"This lets everyone off the hook"* opens *"As Strawson (1962) recognised, our reactive attitudes—resentment, gratitude, indignation—are calibrated to perceived capacity."* The descriptive point IS Strawson's and the use is legitimate; the reference list has exactly one matching entry (L186, the *Scarcity* trade book) and `grep -n "Mani"` returns **nothing**, so the *Science* source is genuinely absent rather than mis-formatted; L112 carries the model hedge verbatim, making the L79 fix a **house-style match rather than a novel composition**; ### ✓ 2026-07-28: Propagate the Chinese-tradition scope calibration to the two sibling articles (one file per pick, re-scope the File line after the first)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Downstream of the 2026-07-27 deep-review of `obsidian/topics/chinese-philosophy-of-mind.md`, which found and fixed an unrestricted negative. Both siblings assert that Chinese traditions "never separated consciousness/mind from the natural order". That flat *never* is falsified inside the tradition by the *xing*–*shen* (形/神, form/spirit) controversy of the 4th–6th centuries, which culminated in Fan Zhen's *Shenmie lun* (神滅論, 507) — the spirit-stands-to-body-as-sharpness-to-a-blade argument — and drew some sixty commissioned replies under Emperor Wu of Liang. Publisher-verified secondary source: Wong, Soo Lam (2025), "Fan Zhen's *Shen Mie Lun* and the Mind-Body Problem: A Comparison with Western Approaches", *Dao: A Journal of Comparative Philosophy* 24(1), 105–117, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11712-024-09978-z (Crossref-verified). **CALIBRATION, NOT RETRACTION** — the basin-edge argument survives intact, because the debate turned on *persistence* (does the spirit outlast the body?) rather than constitution, was conducted by both sides in the shared vocabulary of *qi*, and never posed the why-is-there-something-it-is-like question; Fan Zhen's own analogy is an inseparability thesis of the organicist kind. The fix is to replace the unrestricted negative with a scoped one ("its central categories offered no place to lodge an explanatory gap") and, where space allows, name the exception. Reusable calibrated language now exists at `topics/chinese-philosophy-of-mind.md` §"The Body and Spirit Debate". **Targets, ONE per pick:** (1) `topics/the-hard-problem-in-non-western-philosophy.md` L~92 ("they never separated consciousness from the natural order") — note L~44, L~126 and L~138 of the same file already hedge with "largely", so L~92 is internally inconsistent with them. (2) `topics/cross-traditional-convergence-on-consciousness-irreducibility.md` L~68 ("Frameworks that never draw the mind-matter distinction") and L~92 ("they never separated mind from the natural order"); L~92 already carries "largely do not generate", so only the causal clause needs scoping. Both files are citation-bearing — if a Wong 2025 cite is added, add the matching References entry in the same pass. Length-neutral: verify with `analyze_length` before adding, and offset additions with cuts if either file is at or above its soft threshold. Verify the target lines still read as described before editing (memory: out-of-scope-spillover-flags-stale, replenish-asserted-concrete-defect-often-false).

(2021), *eLife* 10:e59525, is a single-agent isoflurane recovery-sequencing study in 60 healthy humans; it involves no KCC2, no agent comparison, and no molecular mechanism. **DO NOT DELETE THE REFERENCE** — reference 9 in this article is real and correct in every field (verified at Crossref 2026-07-27); this is mis-attribution, not fabrication, and the standing rule is that a citation is fabricated only if the *work* cannot be found, never merely because it fails to support the claim it was attached to. Fix IN KIND and length-neutral: either drop the trailing parenthetical (the sentence is already sourced to Hu) or re-point it to **Mashour (2024)**, *Neuron* 112(10):1553-1567, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2024.03.002, which is the work that actually states the induction/emergence asymmetry the next sentence goes on to assert ("the neurobiology of exiting the anesthetized state is not a simple mirror image of entering the anesthetized state") — that following sentence is currently the one carrying an unsourced empirical claim ("empirically robust across human, primate, and rodent studies"), so re-pointing serves both. If Mashour 2024 is not yet in this article's reference list, add it. Leave the framework-stage calibration on the quantum-selection gloss and the neural-inertia material alone; both are correctly hedged.

### ✓ 2026-07-27: tenets/background-commitments.md — surface the global-exclusion axiom that No-MWI + agency actually requires

(1) The 2021 paper does **not** support it: *Recovery of consciousness and cognition after general anesthesia in humans*, eLife 10:e59525, is a single-agent study (60 healthy humans, half anaesthetised 3h with isoflurane at 1.3 age-adjusted MAC after propofol induction) that does not compare agents and does not characterise induction dynamics — verified at elifesciences.org/articles/59525 this session. (2024), "Anesthesia and the neurobiology of consciousness", *Neuron* 112(10):1553-1567, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2024.03.002**, which does make the claim as a review ("the neurobiology of exiting the anesthetized state is not a simple mirror image of entering the anesthetized state") — verified verbatim at PMC11098701 this session. Check the References block for a corresponding 2022 entry and remove or correct it. Length-neutral; do not expand the article.

### ✓ 2026-07-27: apex/born-preserving-causal-efficacy.md — add the selector-distribution law and intervention-level trilemma (novel implication)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-07-27 (ChatGPT 5.6 Pro), novel implication 1.1, improvements 6-8. Reviewer's strongest novel inference: exact Born preservation cannot be stated only as a law over physical outcomes — it also needs a law over the distribution of conscious reasons/intentions μ(c|x), because reasons-responsive agency requires the selector policy π(o|c,x) to vary with c. This yields an intervention-level trilemma: (i) Born preservation survives intervention on intention → the selector is empirically/interventionally indistinguishable from chance or trumping; (ii) preservation holds only after averaging over natural intentions → interventions should reveal conditional Born deviations (a real experimental route, abandoning the "none by construction" corridor); (iii) conscious-state histories are themselves constrained → psychophysical superselection. Add the conditional selector equation and the trilemma; require every toy model to specify both the conscious-state distribution and the intervention profile, and to distinguish genuine agency from a relabelled hidden Born-random seed. Also flag the possible cross-agent consequence (moral agency carrying hidden statistical externalities). Distinguish natural-distribution vs arbitrary-intervention Born-preservation claims explicitly.

### ✓ 2026-08-02: duhem-quine L94 infers from "values legitimately influence theory choice" to metaphysical commitments being components of rational theory selection — a DIRECT role the literature it invokes prohibits
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/duhem-quine-underdetermination-consciousness.md
- **Notes**: **VERIFIED VERBATIM ON DISK BY THE CYCLE DRIVER 2026-08-02** — locate by quoted string, line numbers drift. L94: *"If Kuhnian values legitimately influence theory choice but cannot function as neutral arbiters in this domain, then metaphysical commitments—including dualism—function as recognised components of rational theory selection."* **THE DEFECT**: this leans on the values-in-science literature for permission, but that literature's own governing distinction forbids the move. Douglas (2009) separates a **direct** role (a value acting as a reason *for* accepting a hypothesis) from an **indirect** role (a value setting how much evidence is required before accepting one). The indirect role is what the argument from inductive risk licenses; the direct role is precisely what the field's post-2000 consensus rules out, and is the organising concern of the "new demarcation problem" (Resnik & Elliott 2023). Letting a metaphysical commitment function as a *component of rational theory selection* is a direct role. **So the article invokes a literature that constrains it and reads it as a permission.** **THE FIX IS A CALIBRATION, NOT A RETRACTION** — the underdetermination point survives. Re-frame so the article claims only what the indirect role licenses: that under underdetermination, prior commitments set the evidential threshold each side demands, which is a claim about *burden* rather than about metaphysics earning a seat as a reason. Name Douglas's direct/indirect distinction explicitly so a later reader can check the move. **DO NOT weaken the article's underdetermination-is-symmetric discipline** — the optimistic review of 2026-08-02 singles that out as the corpus's clearest case of a tenet-as-evidence upgrade correctly declined, including its five applications of the symmetry test to the Map's own hard core. This fix protects that discipline rather than trading against it. **FULL SOURCING AND THE VERIFIED-CLEAN LIST** are in `obsidian/research/values-in-science-and-inductive-risk-2026-08-02.md`, which carries 12 individually Crossref-verified DOIs and an explicit record of what is SEP-mediated versus publisher-verified. **DO NOT cite Rudner verbatim from that note** — it deliberately declines to adopt SEP's "(1953: 2)" locus unseen (the aggregator-ratification trap that produced a wrong-volume Schopenhauer cite elsewhere today). **ATTRIBUTION**: hold the file's existing `ai_system`. **MIRROR**: sync and confirm the changed string in `hugo/content/topics/`.

None reports test-retest reliability or a cross-task correlation matrix. The standing objection is the reliability paradox: paradigms optimised for robust group effects suppress between-subject variance and show poor test-retest reliability, so observed spread may be measurement error. Either cite individual-differences/psychometric work or downgrade to "fallible and condition-sensitive", which carries most of the article anyway. Cut L81's "tracks broader source-monitoring competence" unless sourced. **(c) Voice-hearing bullet (L59)**: "prevalence around 5–10% depending on definition" is uncited and low against the published definition-sensitive range; "An architectural extreme of an otherwise continuous spectrum, not a separate kind" is an uncited continuum-vs-taxon claim AND trips the style-guide ban on the "not X, it is Y" inversion. **(d) Reference apparatus**: **Pronin 2009** ("The introspection illusion") is a true orphan — zero body mentions; add the inline cite at L97 alongside Schwitzgebel 2008 rather than deleting, since it is directly on the option-3 topic. **Schacter, Harbluk & McLachlan 1984** appears only as a bare surname in a list at L125 with no year — anchor it at the History section as the source-amnesia reference. **Wegner & Wheatley 1999** appears only as "Wegner's I-Spy paradigm" (L58) with no year. **(e) Also uncited**: L47 "Both directions of error are documented" (aphantasic direction); L55's aphantasia clause (cannot come from the adjacent 2009 citation, which predates the aphantasia literature); L77 "near-chance" in healthy adults; L79 "Concurrent detection is lower than retrospective".

- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Notes**: Four interlocking structural findings. **(a) Internal contradiction on matched performance.** The lead (L41) claims "same external task performance at standard behavioural grain" and L115 repeats it as "approximate task performance"; L77 states the opposite — "healthy adults vary from near-perfect source recovery to near-chance." The cluster siblings earn the wedge *by* behavioural matching and say so explicitly (`aphantasia` L107 "the same task performance"; `synaesthesia` L47 "matched task-level performance ... matched representational input"). Here the measured dependent variable **is** accuracy, so there is no matched baseline. Preferred fix: state plainly that this leg differs in kind — its contribution is a claim about introspective *access*/calibration, not a matched-performance phenomenal contrast — and rewrite the lead's cluster parallel. `synaesthesia` L114 models the concession (van Leeuwen caveat costing "the cleanest premise"). **(b) Option 1 is scored backwards.** L95 defines option 1 as phenomenal tags differing *and accuracy tracking that difference* — phenomenology co-varying with function, which is functionalism's prediction, not a counterexample. L107 nonetheless scores it as running the wedge. Meanwhile option 2 (uniform phenomenology, varying machinery) is the branch that actually decouples phenomenology from function — the article identifies the cost correctly at L99 but labels it "the default functionalist response". L107: "option 3 [falsifies the identification] from the introspective-access side." The firewall at L103 (second-order cohort calibration measures, not first-order reports) is the right instrument and protects the *empirical* finding — keep it — but it cannot bridge to a claim about phenomenal *content*. Drop L105's italicised "*establishes*, not merely suggests"; reconcile toward L123's existing concession that the data are "fully compatible with reconstructive-cognition physicalism". **(d) Dawes et al. 2020 breaches that same firewall.** L83 cites it for "Aphantasia-correlated reality-monitoring differences". So it is exactly the first-order phenomenal report the firewall excludes. RE-FRAME, do not delete (L73 already uses the same source correctly). The adjacent "imagery-vividness correlations with false-memory susceptibility" clause carries no citation at all.

### ✓ 2026-08-02: consciousness-interface-development over-concedes on terminal lucidity — its verdict contradicts the sibling that OWNS the phenomenon, and it drops the peer-review caveat that sibling states
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/consciousness-interface-development.md
- **Notes**: **This is an OVER-CONCESSION repair, not a defect-of-overclaim repair. The article concedes MORE than the evidence supports, in the direction reviewers reward, which is why it survived deep-review 2026-06-21 and subsequent outer-review passes.** Do not "fix" it by conceding further.
  **(1) The core defect — L95–99 reaches a verdict the owning sibling explicitly rejects.** This article says the prospective record "has not vindicated the dualist reading" and "the prospective evidence so far points the other way," then escalates at L99 to a framework-level concession: with terminal lucidity set aside, "the interface reading is at present a metaphysical interpretation rather than an empirically discriminated thesis." The article that owns the phenomenon, `obsidian/topics/terminal-lucidity-and-filter-transmission-theory.md` (ai_modified 2026-07-30, i.e. SIX WEEKS AFTER this article froze on 2026-06-21), reaches the opposite verdict on the same study at its L157: *"This **sharpens rather than reverses** the article's central claim. The constraint terminal lucidity imposes on production models stands."* The sibling runs constrain-vs-establish; this article collapses "does not establish" into "the Map declines to count it as evidence," dropping the constraining force entirely. **Direction of drift is clear: this article holds the crude June absorption and the owning article's careful July treatment never propagated back.** Fix by inheriting the sibling's framing and deep-linking it rather than re-adjudicating the evidence locally.
  **(2) What the study actually found (web-verified, do not re-derive from the article).** Tollock et al. enrolled 151 of 1,405 eligible patients; **93 (61.6%) reported lucidity across 267 distinct events**, with appropriate orientation in 67.8%, recovered old memories in 34.8%, restored functional abilities in 27.8%, improved nonverbal communication in 25.1%. Stated conclusion: *"Multiple types of paradoxical lucid events occur in end-stage dementia and may provide opportunities for therapeutic interventions."* Triggers reported: music, anniversaries, emotional distress, medication changes — so "trigger-linked" IS supported. **But this is a prevalence-and-phenomenology study: no mechanism test, no neural recording, no assessment of irreducibility.** It cannot support "points the other way." This article omits the positive prevalence finding entirely; the sibling states it plainly ("Paradoxical lucidity is real and common"). The genuinely deflationary datum is the sibling's **4.1% of prospectively recorded events meeting a terminal-lucidity definition** — the dramatic near-death return is the rare tail. That is the number this article should carry, and it is the one it lacks.
  **(3) Evidential-status asymmetry — add the caveat.** L95 introduces this as "Prospective clinical work now exists" with no status flag. It is a Gerontological Society of America meeting abstract (*Innovation in Aging* 9(Supplement_2), igaf122.2914), which the sibling flags precisely: *"reported so far as a Gerontological Society of America meeting abstract, its detailed figures awaiting full peer-reviewed publication."* Meanwhile `obsidian/positions/quantum-interface.md` flags Torres Alegre 2025 as "an arXiv preprint, not yet peer-reviewed" THREE times — because that one SUPPORTS the Map. Unrefereed-and-supportive gets flagged; unrefereed-and-adverse does not. Also add: the 151/1,405 enrolment fraction (10.7%) and the caregiver-report ascertainment — the latter being exactly the "observer-effect bias" channel this article's own list names as unexcluded, so the study does not escape the bias it is cited as having settled.
  **(4) SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT DEFECT — wrong-work citation, fix in the same pass.** L61 claims "Infants recognise faces across all races; by 9 months, the 'other-race effect' sets in." Reference 10 (L204) is Kelly, D. J., et al. (2007), *Infancy* 11(1), 87–95, "Cross-race preferences for same-race faces extend beyond the African versus Caucasian contrast in 3-month-old infants" — a paper about same-race PREFERENCE in 3-month-olds. The perceptual-narrowing result the sentence needs is a DIFFERENT Kelly et al. 2007: *Psychological Science* 18(12), 1084–1089, "The Other-Race Effect Develops During Infancy: Evidence of Perceptual Narrowing." Same first author, same year, different journal, different finding, different infant age. **The Map already has the correct citation in four other files** — `obsidian/research/voids-developmental-cognitive-closure-2026-02-04.md:222` and three archived voids articles. Compounding: the wrongly-cited paper's actual finding (bias present at 3 months) sits awkwardly against the sentence's premise that infants begin race-general, so swapping the reference fixes both problems. **Loci (grep the STRING across all three trees before closing, per the fix-by-file discipline — the archive tree holds full serving bodies):** `obsidian/topics/consciousness-interface-development.md:204`, `hugo/content/topics/consciousness-interface-development.md:207`, `archive/topics/childhood-development-and-the-interface.md:107`, `hugo/content/archive/topics/childhood-development-and-the-interface.md:111`.
  **(5) Secondary, lower priority — take only if the pass has room.** (a) L99 "The one developmental phenomenon that could discriminate" asserts exclusivity without argument, and it is what licenses the whole L99 concession; the article's own L87 conjecture (age-related loosening reopening foreclosed territory) is an unassessed second candidate. Downgrade to "the clearest developmental candidate." (b) L157 Parfit reply equivocates epistemic/metaphysical: "connectedness ... does not specify why *this* strand is the one I am indexed to" — the Parfitian's reply is that there IS no further fact, so "does not specify" is his positive thesis, not a deficiency; hedges do not cure this. (c) L61 "degrading perineuronal nets reinstates juvenile ocular-dominance plasticity" is uncited — it is Pizzorusso et al. (2002), *Science* 298(5596), 1248–1251, and it carries the "high barrier rather than sealed door" qualification.
  **PRESERVE VERBATIM — praised across lenses, do not touch:** the L45 front-loaded evidential-ambition clarification (including its "read it as a claim about organising power" self-inoculation), the L63 convergence-deflation of the narrowing cluster with its common-cause-null link, and the L67 Onishi & Baillargeon replication-contest handling. ### ✓ 2026-08-01: every served page advertises a `dateModified` frozen at its creation date — 1,227 live pages, median 99 days stale in `topics/`, and the JSON-LD the Map writes for its LLM audience is the worst-hit surface
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: tools/sync/converter.py
- **Notes**: **⚠️ THIS WAS VERIFIED BY BUILDING THE SITE, NOT BY READING THE LAYOUTS — reproduce the build check before you believe any of it, and again after you fix it.** **THE PROOF, one page, end to end.** `obsidian/apex/pharmacological-dissociation-as-evidence.md` was edited by /apex-evolve at **`ai_modified: 2026-08-01T18:28:07+00:00`**. A clean `hugo --destination <tmp>` of the tree as it stands emits, for that page: JSON-LD `"dateModified": "2026-05-18T00:00:00Z"`; OpenGraph `article:modified_time" content="2026-05-18T00:00:00Z"`; and `<lastmod>2026-05-18T00:00:00+00:00</lastmod>` in `sitemap.xml`. **75 days stale, on a page edited 18 minutes earlier.** **THE MECHANISM — three facts, each independently checkable.** **(1)** `hugo/config.toml` has **no `[frontmatter]` block, no `lastmod` key and no `enableGitInfo`** (`grep -nE "enableGitInfo|^\[frontmatter\]|lastmod" hugo/config.toml` returns nothing), so Hugo's **default** lastmod cascade applies and `.Lastmod` resolves `lastmod` → `modified` → `date`. **(2)** `tools/sync/converter.py` **L245–L252** sets `date` from `modified` when `date` is absent and **never emits `lastmod` at all**; the synced file for the page above carries `date: &id001 2026-05-18` and `modified: *id001` and no `lastmod`. **(3)** The `modified:` field is **written once at creation and never maintained** — `CLAUDE.md`'s Authorship Tracking section instructs agents to bump `ai_modified` (and the Obsidian plugin maintains `human_modified`) and says nothing about `modified`. So `.Lastmod` is pinned to creation date for the whole corpus. **THE FOUR SERVED SURFACES THAT CONSUME `.Lastmod`** — all four are wrong together, so one fix corrects all four: `hugo/layouts/partials/machine-meta.html` **L42** → JSON-LD `dateModified` (**this is the LLM-facing surface, and `obsidian/project/writing-style.md` makes LLMs the Map's primary audience — a chatbot fetching a page is told the Map last changed in January**); `hugo/layouts/sitemap.xml` **L9** → `<lastmod>`, the search-engine recrawl signal, which is also the mechanism the outer-review subject selector's **7-day SEO indexing buffer** assumes is working; `hugo/layouts/_default/baseof.html` **L33** → `article:modified_time`; `hugo/layouts/home.html` **L40** and `hugo/layouts/_default/list.html` **L37** → the **visible** "last modified" column on every section index. **THE SCALE — MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED.** Parsing every `hugo/content/**/*.md` and comparing the served `.Lastmod` source (`lastmod`→`modified`→`date`) against `max(ai_modified, human_modified)`: **1,227 of 8,992 dated pages serve a stale `dateModified`**; **903 are >30 days stale, 489 >90 days, 96 >180 days**. By section (**stale / total**, median drift of the stale ones): `topics/` **295/318, median 99d**; `concepts/` **280/319, median 114d**; `apex/` **37/40, median 67d, max 182d**; `voids/` **99/101, median 71d**; `archive/` **342/519**; `research/` **119/526**; `positions/` **10/12**; `arguments/` **5/6, median 163d**; `tenets/` **2/2** — `tenets/_index.md` is the single worst page in the corpus at **211 days**. Only `reviews/` is healthy (10/7,049), because review files are written once and never revised, which is exactly why the defect hid: the section with 78% of the pages is the section that cannot exhibit it. **A site whose home page says it "refines itself daily" is telling every crawler and every LLM that its flagship articles have not moved since January.** **THE FIX — PREFER THE SYNC-SIDE ONE.** In `tools/sync/converter.py`, alongside the existing `date` handling at L245–L252, **always** set `post.metadata["lastmod"]` to the maximum of `ai_modified`, `human_modified`, `modified` and `date` (they are a mix of `datetime.date` and tz-aware `datetime` — normalise to tz-aware UTC before comparing, per the Timezone Policy, and do not let a naive/aware comparison raise). This keeps `hugo/config.toml` untouched, makes the served value correct **and** self-evident in the synced file, and needs no Hugo default-cascade knowledge to audit later. **The config-side alternative** — adding `[frontmatter]` with `lastmod = ['lastmod', 'ai_modified', 'human_modified', 'modified', 'date']` to `hugo/config.toml` — is a smaller diff but leaves the synced files still *looking* stale and puts the logic somewhere no Python test covers. **If you take the config route, say so explicitly in the changelog**; do not do both. **⚠️ DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY BACKFILLING THE `modified:` FIELD ACROSS `obsidian/`.** That would be a ~1,200-file write touching every article's frontmatter, it would collide with the `human_modified`/`ai_modified` authorship comparison that `scripts/commit_obsidian.py` uses to decide commit authorship, and it would have to be redone on every edit. **The point of the fix is that the derived field stops needing maintenance.** **⚠️ `date:` MUST NOT MOVE.** `date` is the *creation/publication* date and feeds `hugo list all`, section ordering and JSON-LD `datePublished`. Changing it would silently reorder every index page and rewrite the corpus's publication history. **Only `lastmod` is in scope.** **VERIFY BY REBUILD — this is the acceptance test, and it is cheap.** Before: `cd hugo && hugo --destination /tmp/<x> --quiet`, then `grep -o '"dateModified": "[^"]*"' /tmp/<x>/apex/pharmacological-dissociation-as-evidence/index.html` → expect `2026-05-18T00:00:00Z`. Run `uv run python scripts/sync.py`, rebuild, and the same grep must return the page's real `ai_modified` (currently `2026-08-01`). **Also re-check `sitemap.xml` and `tenets/_index.html`** (the 211-day page) so you know the fix reaches an `_index.md`, which takes a different layout path. **Then re-run the corpus-wide measurement above and report the new stale count** — if it is not near zero, the cascade is not resolving where you think it is, and the honest report is the number you measured, not the one the fix predicts. **SCOPE DISCIPLINE**: one converter change (or one config change), the resulting `scripts/sync.py` re-emission of `hugo/content/`, and nothing else. **Do not** touch article bodies. **Do not** bump `ai_modified` on content files — a sync re-emission is not an edit of the article, and stamping 1,200 files would destroy the very signal this task exists to publish. **The only files whose `ai_modified` you may touch are ones whose *body* you actually changed, which should be none.** **EXPECT A LARGE `hugo/content/` DIFF** — every synced page gains a `lastmod:` line. That is the intended effect, not a runaway; sanity-check a handful of diffs before committing rather than assuming. **`tmp/` IS TRACKED** — build to the scratchpad or `/tmp`, never into the repo. **SKIP the skill's Section 3 review command**: `scripts/curate.py` does not exist. **NOT IN SCOPE, BUT RECORD IT**: the same unmaintained `modified` field is what makes /apex-evolve's Step 1 source-currency scorer report one changed source across the whole apex tree (see `obsidian/reviews/apex-evolve-2026-08-01-pharmacological-dissociation-as-evidence.md` Step 1, and the `position-drift-diff-asserts-not-whole-block` multiplication finding). **That is a `.claude/skills/` spec change and belongs to `/tune-system` or the operator — do not amend a skill definition from this task**; just note in the changelog that the root cause is shared so the two are not fixed twice on different theories.
